summary: Andrew Glass works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Washington (MA 2000, PhD 2006) under doctoral supervisor Richard Salomon, at Bukkyo University, and under Mark Allon, Ulrich Pagel, Sonam Wanggyal, and Gudrun Melzer.

Andrew Goudie (born 1945) is a scholar in history and archaeology. He studied at Dean Close School and Trinity Hall, Cambridge, and served as a professor at the University of Oxford from 1970 to 2014.
Andrew J. Nicholson specializes in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under the traditional teacher Shrinarayan Mishra and holds a post at Stony Brook University.

Andrew Olendzki works in Buddhist studies. He studied at Lancaster University and under Masatoshi Nagatomi, later serving at the Insight Meditation Society, Barre Center for Buddhist Studies (attested 2003–2014), and Mind & Life Institute (attested 2014).

Andrew P. Tuck works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Princeton University and was taught by Victor Preller, Jeffrey Stout, William E. Kennick, Robert A. F. Thurman, John Pemberton, D. Dennis Hudson, Daniel H. H. Ingalls, Alan Sponberg, and Richard Rorty.

Andrew Quintman works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jay L. Garfield and served as an assistant professor in the Department of Religious Studies at Yale University (attested 2015).
Andrew Sihler (born 1941) is a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Harvard and Yale under Warren Cowgill, and held a post at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from approximately 1967 to 1998.
Andrew Watsky (born 1957) is a scholar of Japanology and history/archaeology. He studied at Oberlin College and Princeton University, and held a post at Vassar College from circa 1994 to 2008.
Andrew William Kennedy works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Leeds (attested 2006) under doctoral supervisors Philip A. Mellor and Kim Knott.

Andrey Klebanov specializes in Indology and linguistics. He earned an MA and PhD at the University of Hamburg under Harunaga Isaacson, worked there (attested 2015), and served as a professor at Kyoto University (attested 2018–2021).

Andrey Terentyev (born 1948) specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied philosophy at Saint Petersburg State University from circa 1970 to 1975 and held a post at the Museum of History of Religion from approximately 1978 to 1998.

Andrzej Gawroński (1885–1927) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Lviv and University of Leipzig, later holding posts at Jagiellonian University (1916–1917) and the University of Lviv as a full professor (1917).

András Róna-Tas (born 1931) is a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, later serving as professor at the University of Szeged (1968–2002).

André Bareau (1921–1993) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at the Sorbonne, EPHE, and Collège de France under Jean Filliozat and Paul Demiéville, later holding posts at the CNRS, EPHE, and Collège de France.

André Caquot (1923–2004) specialized in religious studies and linguistics. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure and EPHE, later holding positions at the EPHE, University of Strasbourg, University of Paris, and Collège de France (1972–1994).

André Couture (born 1945) is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at Laval University, EPHE, and Paris-Sorbonne University, and held an academic post at Laval University from approximately 1979 to 2011.

André Godard (1881–1965) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the École Nationale Supérieure des Beaux-Arts and held a post at the University of Tehran from circa 1934 to 1953.

André Martinet (1908–1999) was a linguist who studied at the Sorbonne and University of Berlin under Antoine Meillet. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, Columbia University, and the University of Paris.
André Mazon (1881–1967) was a linguist who studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris and the University of Prague. He held a post at the Collège de France from 1923 to 1951.

André Padoux (1920–2017) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Paris under Louis Renou and Olivier Lacombe, directed the Institut Français Frankfurt, and served as Directeur de Recherche at the CNRS.
